observation: Fresh main already made addEvidence() authoritative over evidence id and timestamp, but durable mission reads still accepted arbitrary evidence entries. A persisted mission could therefore be rewritten with forged/missing evidence identity metadata and still be treated as valid, weakening the user-visible verification trail.
changes: Validate every durable mission evidence item as an object with store-owned mev-<12 lowercase hex> identity and a non-empty timestamp.
Publish that minimal evidence identity envelope in Autonomous Mission v0.1 while leaving payload fields extensible.
Extend the existing evidence-identity regression from write-time authority to durable-read tamper rejection.

verification.pre_fix_source_contract_replay: EXPECTED FAIL: mission evidence was checked only as an array; forged ids, empty timestamps, and null entries were readable.
verification.post_fix_source_contract_replay: PASS: durable evidence now preserves the same identity/timestamp envelope already generated by addEvidence(), while arbitrary payload fields remain allowed.
verification.focused_regression_contract: Existing mission evidence tests still cover caller id/time override resistance; the new case covers persisted forged id, empty timestamp, and null entry rejection.
verification.hosted_runtime: Developer Execution Runtime remained unavailable with HTTP 502; no hosted full-suite pass is claimed.

truth_boundary: This cycle does not introduce signatures, MACs, append-only storage, or a trust root. It only makes durable reads honor the identity envelope already owned by the existing evidence writer.
